Synthetic five-step standard-input workbooks

Every identifier, MAC, address, device name and engineering quantity is synthetic.
No customer workbook or credentials were copied into these fixtures.

Generate from dev/backend:
  go run ./cmd/engineering-fixtures
Run native XLSX and independent model expectations:
  go test ./internal/engineering -run 'Test(FiveStepXLSX|StandardXLSX)'

expected.json contains independently stated engineering expectations. It is not
an acceptance report. Rules/policy references must be explicitly installed and
reviewed in an isolated test project; fixture names do not grant approval.

Current scope: all five fixed-input steps passed one continuous isolated real
API/PostgreSQL/MinIO/review/Outbox/CMDB/chart-data acceptance. Step 3 includes
approved project rules, explicit channels, per-segment cable plans, standard
stock selection, physical-port optic dedup and material/workload quantities.
The new unstructured-source triage and scoped extraction Agent is not implemented.
Core IPv4 BGP is the tested logical profile; no real device or power operations.
Evidence: docs/intelligent-deployment/FIVE-STEP-CHAIN-ACCEPTANCE-20261102.json.

When retaining multiple test projects, namespace synthetic SN/MAC/site/room/rack
codes consistently across all five files; CMDB unique identity guards still apply.
Rule references are code@version or UUID@version. Install and approve the three
cabling fixture rules in the isolated project; downloading a file grants no approval.
